n: From the wilderness of Paran, close to Canaan, the Lord speaks to Moses about scouting the land. Deuteronomy 1:22 adds that the people first requested it.
Send twelve men, a leader from each tribe, to explore Canaan—the land God is already giving them.

f.g: Explore, scout out.

f.w: which I give unto the children of Israel

n: Moses sends them, all respected leaders—though different men from the tribal chiefs of chapter 1.

f.g: Leaders.

n: From Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur.
From Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori.
From Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh, who will become a hero of faith in this story.
From Issachar: Igal son of Joseph.
From Ephraim: Oshea (Hoshea) son of Nun—better known as Joshua.

f.g: Hoshea means “salvation.”

n: From Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu.
From Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi.
From Manasseh (one of Joseph’s two tribes): Gaddi son of Susi.
From Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli.
From Asher: Sethur son of Michael.
From Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi.
From Gad: Geuel son of Machi. Of these twelve names, only Caleb and Joshua are remembered for faith.
Moses renames Hoshea as Jehoshua (Joshua), “Jehovah is salvation.” Jesus is the Greek form of this same name.

f.g: Hebrew Yehoshua, “Jehovah saves”; in Greek, Iēsous (Jesus).

n: Moses sends them north through the Negev (the dry south) and into the hill country.

f.g: Hebrew negev, the dry southern region of Canaan.

n: Their mission: learn about the land and its people—strong or weak, few or many.
Is the land good? Are the cities open camps or fortified?

f.g: Fortified cities.

n: Is the soil rich? Are there trees? Be courageous and bring back fruit. It was the season of first-ripe grapes, around late summer.

f.g: Fertile or poor.

n: They explore from the wilderness of Zin in the south to Rehob near Hamath in the far north—the full length of the land.

f.g: Desert area on Canaan’s southern border.
A city in Syria; “the entrance of Hamath” marked Israel’s ideal northern border.

n: At Hebron they see the descendants of Anak, a people known for great size. Hebron was ancient—built seven years before Zoan in Egypt—and was where Abraham was buried.

f.g: The Anakim, a clan famed for their height.
Tanis, a city in Egypt’s delta.

n: At the Eshcol valley they cut a grape cluster so large two men carried it on a pole, plus pomegranates and figs. The land was truly abundant.

f.w: bare it between two upon a staff
f.g: Carried it on a pole between two men.

n: The valley was named Eshcol, meaning “cluster.”

f.g: Hebrew for “cluster” of grapes.

n: They return after forty days. Forty will soon become an important number in Israel’s story.
They report to Moses, Aaron, and everyone at Kadesh in Paran, showing the fruit.

f.g: Kadesh-barnea, an oasis that became Israel’s base in the wilderness.

n: Their report starts well: the land does flow with milk and honey—just as God promised. Here is the proof.
“Nevertheless”—the turning word. The people are strong, the cities walled, and the Anakim are there. They see the obstacles more than the promise.

f.g: However, but.

n: They list the nations: Amalekites in the south, Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites in the hills, and Canaanites along the coast and Jordan.

f.g: The people living in Jerusalem (Jebus).

n: Caleb quiets the crowd: “Let us go up at once and take it—we can certainly do it!” He trusts God’s promise over appearances.

f.g: Quieted.

f.w: we are well able to overcome it

n: But the other spies (except Joshua) say, “We can’t—they are stronger than we are.” They leave God out of the equation.
They spread a bad report: the land “eats up its inhabitants”—perhaps meaning it is constantly fought over—and the people are huge. Fear exaggerates.

f.g: A discouraging, slanderous report.
Devours those who live there—perhaps through warfare or hardship.

n: “We saw the giants... and we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so we were in theirs.” How they saw themselves shaped how they thought others saw them. Faith would have measured the giants against God instead.

f.g: Hebrew nephilim, an ancient term for people of great size.
